dedupe_keys.name: bts supply chain and freight indicators

description: The Supply Chain and Freight Indicators dataset is produced by an interagency working group led by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics, with the DOT modal administrations and the Departments of Agriculture, Energy, Commerce and Labor, to give timely information on supply chain activity. It covers four areas: port data inside the gate, port data outside the gate, freight movement, and transportation labour and capacity tightness. Each row gives an indicator, date and year, one or two measures with descriptions, a value, units, notes and the source; the table has 26,652 rows, and Canadian Pacific Kansas City railway data are updated weekly from May 2025. Coverage is national. The data are free and in the public domain on data.bts.gov, with CSV and JSON export and an API, and charts on the BTS freight indicators page. Caveats: indicators come from many sources with different frequencies and definitions, and some series stop or change when reporters merge, as with the Canadian Pacific and Kansas City Southern railways. The indicators support monitoring and calibration of freight network flow and capacity planning models, and baselines for supply chain disruption and resilience studies. It complements the BTS port performance data and the Freight Analysis Framework.
